newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S BKD BANK SEES FURTHER EXPANSION.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S BKD BANK SEES FURTHER EXPANSION.

text.p: Hungary's BNP-Dresdner Bank (Hungaria) Rt (BKD) said on Monday it raised its share capital to 3.5 billion forints from 2.0 billion forints to increase sources for further expansion in the Hungarian market.

"We asked our board of directors and our shareholders to increase our capital to be more competitive...," Hartmut Welk, BKD's Deputy General Manager, told a news conference, following the bank's extraordinary general meeting today.
"The capital increase will provide a solid basis for future expansion," the bank said in a statement.
The shares will be offered to Banque National de Paris and Dresdner Bank in proportion to their existing 50-50 percent stakes, it said.
BKD looks forward to expanding to non-banking areas as well and hopes to complete talks to buy a brokerage house.
"We're still negotiating with one broker," Welk said. "We did not finish the negotiations, as usual it's question of money," he said, expressing hopes that talks can be completed by year end.

In January 1996 BKD said it was considering buying Microbroker Kft, a Budapest Stock Exchange bourse member brokerage. However, Welk told Reuters the current talks were with another broker which he declined to name.

Welk said BKD posted a pre-tax profit of 936 million forints and an after-tax profit of 767 million in the first nine months of 1996. These figures compare to 688 million and 563 million respectively, in 1995.
The bank aims to post an after-tax profit of one billion forints for thge year, Welk said.
